issue.body:
## Summary
- Added optional `duration_ms` and `waveform` fields to MDK media references and uploads so audio attachments can carry typed display metadata.
- Updated IMETA parsing to accept best-effort `duration` and `waveform` fields without breaking required MIP-04 decryption inputs.
- Updated IMETA building and UniFFI bindings so downstream apps can round-trip the new metadata.
- Kept existing image/video/file IMETA behavior intact and left audio decoding/UI policy out of MDK.

## Testing
- Added unit coverage for valid audio metadata, missing optional metadata, malformed duration, malformed waveform, required-field failures, and builder round-trips.
- Ran `cargo test -p mdk-core encrypted_media --features mip04`.
- Ran `cargo test -p mdk-uniffi test_create_and_parse_imeta_tag_round_trip --all-features`.
- Ran `cargo check --all-features` and `just check`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
This PR adds optional audio display metadata to MIP-04 IMETA tags so audio attachments can carry typed presentation information (duration and a lightweight waveform) while preserving existing decryption inputs and backward compatibility. It updates core parsing/formatting and UniFFI bindings so downstream apps can round-trip the new metadata without changing required MIP-04 fields.

**What changed**:
- Added optional fields `duration_ms: Option<u64>` and `waveform: Option<Vec<u8>>` to EncryptedMediaUpload and MediaReference in mdk-core.
- Extended EncryptedMediaManager parsing and tag-building to accept/emit `duration` (seconds with optional fractional part) and `waveform` (whitespace-separated 0..=100 samples) as best-effort display metadata, enforcing a maximum sample count and sample-range/format validation.
- Updated mdk-uniffi records (EncryptedMediaUploadResult and MediaReferenceRecord) and conversion code to carry `duration_ms` and `waveform` across the FFI boundary.
- IMETA generation conditionally emits the new fields when present; existing image/video/file IMETA behavior unchanged and audio decoding/UI policy remains out of MDK.

**Protocol changes**:
- MIP-04 IMETA tags now optionally support NIP-A0 `duration` and `waveform` entries as display-only metadata; required encryption/decryption fields are unchanged and still enforced.

**API surface**:
- Public struct fields added: EncryptedMediaUpload::duration_ms, EncryptedMediaUpload::waveform, MediaReference::duration_ms, MediaReference::waveform (mdk-core).
- UniFFI/FFI record fields added: EncryptedMediaUploadResult::duration_ms, EncryptedMediaUploadResult::waveform, MediaReferenceRecord::duration_ms, MediaReferenceRecord::waveform (mdk-uniffi).
- No breaking changes: all new fields are optional and default to None.

**Testing**:
- Added/updated unit tests covering valid audio metadata, missing optional metadata, malformed duration, malformed waveform, required-field enforcement, and builder/round-trip behavior.
- Verified with: cargo test -p mdk-core encrypted_media --features mip04; cargo test -p mdk-uniffi test_create_and_parse_imeta_tag_round_trip --all-features; and cargo check --all-features.

- Added optional `duration_ms` and `waveform` fields to MDK media references and uploads so audio attachments can carry typed display metadata.
- Updated IMETA parsing to accept best-effort `duration` and `waveform` fields without breaking required MIP-04 decryption inputs.
- Updated IMETA building and UniFFI bindings so downstream apps can round-trip the new metadata.
- Kept existing image/video/file IMETA behavior intact and left audio decoding/UI policy out of MDK.

## Testing
- Added unit coverage for valid audio metadata, missing optional metadata, malformed duration, malformed waveform, required-field failures, and builder round-trips.
- Ran `cargo test -p mdk-core encrypted_media --features mip04`.
- Ran `cargo test -p mdk-uniffi test_create_and_parse_imeta_tag_round_trip --all-features`.
- Ran `cargo check --all-features` and `just check`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
This PR adds optional audio display metadata to MIP-04 IMETA tags so audio attachments can carry typed presentation information (duration and a lightweight waveform) while preserving existing decryption inputs and backward compatibility. It updates core parsing/formatting and UniFFI bindings so downstream apps can round-trip the new metadata without changing required MIP-04 fields.

**What changed**:
- Added optional fields `duration_ms: Option<u64>` and `waveform: Option<Vec<u8>>` to EncryptedMediaUpload and MediaReference in mdk-core.
- Extended EncryptedMediaManager parsing and tag-building to accept/emit `duration` (seconds with optional fractional part) and `waveform` (whitespace-separated 0..=100 samples) as best-effort display metadata, enforcing a maximum sample count and sample-range/format validation.
- Updated mdk-uniffi records (EncryptedMediaUploadResult and MediaReferenceRecord) and conversion code to carry `duration_ms` and `waveform` across the FFI boundary.
- IMETA generation conditionally emits the new fields when present; existing image/video/file IMETA behavior unchanged and audio decoding/UI policy remains out of MDK.

**Protocol changes**:
- MIP-04 IMETA tags now optionally support NIP-A0 `duration` and `waveform` entries as display-only metadata; required encryption/decryption fields are unchanged and still enforced.

**API surface**:
- Public struct fields added: EncryptedMediaUpload::duration_ms, EncryptedMediaUpload::waveform, MediaReference::duration_ms, MediaReference::waveform (mdk-core).
- UniFFI/FFI record fields added: EncryptedMediaUploadResult::duration_ms, EncryptedMediaUploadResult::waveform, MediaReferenceRecord::duration_ms, MediaReferenceRecord::waveform (mdk-uniffi).
- No breaking changes: all new fields are optional and default to None.

**Testing**:
- Added/updated unit tests covering valid audio metadata, missing optional metadata, malformed duration, malformed waveform, required-field enforcement, and builder/round-trip behavior.
- Verified with: cargo test -p mdk-core encrypted_media --features mip04; cargo test -p mdk-uniffi test_create_and_parse_imeta_tag_round_trip --all-features; and cargo check --all-features.

**`welcome_group_index` now bypasses the welcome cache size bound.**

This stores a non-evicting `wrapper_event_id -> mls_group_id` entry for **every** saved welcome, so a stream of distinct welcomes can grow memory indefinitely even after `welcomes_cache` evicts the payloads. That weakens the backend’s documented cache-based memory protection. Prefer recording this association only for entries that actually become `ProcessedWelcome`s, or co-locating the group linkage with the non-evicting processed-welcome record instead.

unconditional inner.welcome_group_index.insert(wrapper_event_id, mls_group_id)
stores a mapping for every saved welcome and can grow without bound; change this
so the mapping is only recorded for items that become ProcessedWelcome (or move
the mapping into the non-evicting processed_welcomes record) instead of

alongside the processed_welcome entry), so delete_group can still look up group

issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/6db0e33277f9d54c9fb9a6f7793dc813e0b4bf406b804bd368d521c0a9fd1cbc.jpg) Closes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#68. `MdkStorageProvider::delete_group` left every `processed_welcomes` row behind in both the sqlite and memory backends. Two consequences fell out of that: - **Data retention.** After a marmot "completely" deleted a group, their store still held `wrapper_event_id`, `welcome_event_id`, `processed_at`, `state`, and the unsanitized `failure_reason` for every welcome they ever processed for that group, linkable forever, even if the group was never recreated. - **Dedup breakage.** The welcome dedup path in `welcomes::process_welcome` returns early on any wrapper id that already has a `ProcessedWelcome` row. With the row surviving, a re-processed kind:1059 (relay replay, app reinstall from backup, client retry) hit the stale row, looked up the now-missing `Welcome`, and surfaced `Error::Welcome("welcome record missing for processed welcome")`, which points far from the real cause. `processed_welcomes` has no `mls_group_id` column and no FK to `groups`, so cleanup joins through `welcomes` by `wrapper_event_id`. The sqlite delete runs before the existing `DELETE FROM welcomes` so the subquery still resolves. The memory backend collects each welcome's `wrapper_event_id` during the welcomes_cache scan and pops the matching `processed_welcomes_cache` entries. ## Changes - `crates/mdk-sqlite-storage/src/lib.rs`: `delete_group` now scrubs `processed_welcomes` via `DELETE FROM processed_welcomes WHERE wrapper_event_id IN (SELECT wrapper_event_id FROM welcomes WHERE mls_group_id = ?)`, ordered before the welcomes delete. - `crates/mdk-memory-storage/src/lib.rs`: `delete_group` collects `wrapper_event_id`s from `welcomes_cache` and pops matching entries from `processed_welcomes_cache`. - `crates/mdk-core/src/groups.rs`: `MDK::delete_group` docstring lists welcome and processed welcome records. - Regression tests in both backends seed a Welcome with a known `wrapper_event_id` plus a `ProcessedWelcome` referencing it, then assert the row is gone after `delete_group`. ## Verification - `cargo test -p mdk-sqlite-storage delete_group`: 4 passed. - `cargo test -p mdk-memory-storage delete_group`: 4 passed. - `just precommit`: fmt, docs, clippy (stable + msrv), all-features tests, no-features tests, mip04 tests, cargo audit, all green. ## Notes Schema is unchanged on purpose. Adding `mls_group_id` to `processed_welcomes` would need a migration and call-site plumbing for marginal benefit; the JOIN approach matches what `welcomes` and `processed_messages` already do for group-scoped cleanup. --- This PR fixes a bug where MdkStorageProvider::delete_group failed to remove processed_welcomes records in the sqlite and memory backends, which could retain processed-welcome metadata and break welcome deduplication after group deletion. The change ensures processed_welcomes are scrubbed when a group is deleted, updates documentation, and adds regression tests verifying the behavior. **What changed**: - mdk-sqlite-storage: delete_group now deletes processed_welcomes rows via DELETE FROM processed_welcomes WHERE wrapper_event_id IN (SELECT wrapper_event_id FROM welcomes WHERE mls_group_id = ?), executed before deleting welcomes inside the existing transaction. - mdk-memory-storage: added a non-evicting welcome_group_index mapping wrapper_event_id → GroupId maintained by save_processed_welcome and used by delete_group to remove matching entries from processed_welcomes_cache; snapshot/restore updated to persist the index. - mdk-core: updated MDK::delete_group docstring to explicitly list welcome and processed-welcome records as removed. - Tests and changelogs: added regression tests for both backends that seed a Welcome + ProcessedWelcome, call delete_group, and assert processed_welcomes removal; changelogs updated. **Security impact**: - Improves privacy by removing persistent ProcessedWelcome metadata (wrapper_event_id, welcome_event_id, processed_at, state, unsanitized failure_reason) when a group is deleted and prevents deduplication errors; no changes to cryptography, key handling, SQLCipher configuration, or file permissions. **Protocol changes**: - None to MLS protocol, Nostr integrations, or MIP behavior. **API surface**: - No breaking changes to public APIs or exported types. - Storage schema unchanged (no new DB column); memory snapshot gained a crate-visible welcome_group_index field to persist the wrapper_event_id → GroupId index across snapshots. **Testing**: - New regression tests added for sqlite and memory storage validating processed_welcomes removal (sqlite test includes a direct SQL count check); reported local test runs and precommit checks passed.
